newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end marginally lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end marginally lower.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a volatile day marginally lower on worries about higher interest rate hikes, lower bond prices and an easier Wall Street opening.
Dealers said demand by U.S. and U.K. investment funds for bank shares underpinned the market.
"There has been a change of heart," a trader noted with respect to the renewed interest in banks. A weaker U.S. dollar also pressured some shares.
Sentiment was nervous ahead of the March meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve with investors increasingly worried about an interest rate hike.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closed down 0.9 points, or 0.02 percent, at 4,676.2 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 5.87 points, or 0.2 percent, to end at 2,954.45.
Trade was also influenced by derivatives-linked transactions, a dealer said.

Swiss Bank Corp was the major gainer in the blue-chip segment, rising seven francs to 310. The bank released 1996 results which were seen largely in line with expectations. Credit Suisse Group extended recent gains, closing up 1.50 francs at 171.50. Union Bank of Switzerland slid seven francs to 1,348.
Novartis were up 13 francs, or 0.73 percent, to 1,788. Roche fell 150 francs to 12,480. Stocks of chemical firm Clariant slipped 27 francs to 711.
The shares were probably pressured by a slide of more than 10 percent of Hoechst in Frankfurt on lower-than-expected key data, one dealer noted. Hoechst holds a stake in Clariant.
Alusuisse, Holderbank, SMH and Nestle were among the day's losers.
